# Explicit session authorization, not a guard bypass

- A user may explicitly authorize one supervised development session covering verified routine operations. Record its scope and limits; do not treat this file, a USB descriptor, an intent or a previous session's grant as authorization. Preserve the legacy manual workflow.
- `AUTO_VERIFIED` is limited to the approved model, VID:PID `734c:5530`, current boot/attachment generation/owner, exact reviewed firmware and frontend plans, and K36 DVB-T2 `594000000 Hz` / `8000000 Hz` / AUTO on observed chip `0x197`. `EXPERIMENTAL_DIAGNOSTIC` adds only specifically allowlisted receive-transport experiments; it never authorizes arbitrary register writes.
- Lock firmware to SHA-256 `b97cf208bb586f706b26aa5450de6bb97375a3e3eabe833cddb0ae3a4f69d0dc`, 8192 bytes and the source-confirmed 132-transfer dual-reset RAM plan. Read fresh raw descriptors and Android metadata. Upload at most once per valid FX2_DEFAULT attachment; skip upload for operational profiles. Never bundle firmware into APKs or infer its redistribution license.
- Separate session consent from single-use attempt consumption. Use a new versioned namespace; never reset, rewrite, rearm or reuse Phase 2.9–3.1 consumed stores or historic firmware ledger entries. Audit and durably consume each fresh attempt before its first write, while allowing the validated session to issue that attempt without another UI approval.
- Android can reuse the same USB path/id after an OTG power-cycle. Never treat a new session UUID as proof of a new physical attachment. If no continuous verified attach observer exists, a recovery epoch must be explicitly tied to a user-confirmed physical recovery, remain fixed across retries/restarts, and be bound into the immutable grant and append-only upload key. Do not silently mint a new epoch, remove old records or rearm an uncertain attachment; malformed/missing recovery provenance must fail closed.
- Prove the exact allowlist and dry-run guards with fake-only tests before arming live mode. Bind plans, firmware hash, boot identity and fresh attachment/owner; reject corrupt state, changed parameters, ambiguous devices and stale generations. Keep Android UsbManager permission mandatory; a system permission dialog may require one user action, never a shell/root bypass.
- Bound each session to at most five minutes, preserve the two-second host-heartbeat freshness check and existing per-call/program deadlines, and cap transport variants, reads and bytes. Provide STOP in the foreground UI and host helper; stop on foreground/host/permission loss, detach, deadline or unexpected native result. Do not start services through reboot, open ports or keep unattended remote control running.
- Native I/O must use the owned claimed connection, with cancellation, drain and deferred cleanup. Never force-close an active syscall. After partial/uncertain firmware I/O, stop all writes for that attachment; request physical recovery rather than retry, CPU-release or reset. Re-enumeration requires fresh permission/owner evidence, never a stale handle.
- EEPROM/flash, satellite/LNB/antenna DC, mode changes, driver changes, USB/IP ownership, power-cycle and unreviewed vendor writes are excluded. A new experimental scope requires a separate bounded decision, not one approval per known routine transaction.
- Keep raw TS, firmware, device identities, grants, ledgers and traces outside Git. Report measured bytes, errno, packet structure and quality separately; neither lock nor Windows TS nor fake tests prove Android `TS_SMOKE_PASS`.
